objective.title: Qualify typed IR ADR with phase-aware M1 baseline gate verification

declared.summary: Complete the first M2 architecture spike by comparing OpenMath 2.0 Revision 2, W3C Content MathML 4 and candidate ASTs, selecting a bounded immutable provider-neutral typed model, and qualifying a structured five-case exact semantic-loss ledger plus a read-only C# decision validator.
declared.value: Fixes the future IR's exact/approximate, unit, scope, assumption and matrix semantics before implementation, reusing the qualified ExactRational primitive and explicitly rejecting lossy silent simplification or provider coupling.
debtChanges: No M2 IR library, parser, codec or OpenMath/Content MathML exporter is created by this spike; M2-W01-C02 owns compiled RED/GREEN contracts and package qualification.
Numeric resource budgets, symbolic substitution and canonical structural hashing are proposed policies, not demonstrated product capabilities; no dynamic provider registry is authorized.
External AURA adoption remains draft/untransmitted. All M1 exact unit and package contracts remain unchanged.

Retry 0 was a pre-attempt ProjectPlan refusal: M1 left no active hierarchy, so ActivateReadyContinuation was not admissible. Retry 1 initializes M2 by exact legal not-ready/ready/in-progress transitions without changing science, validators or scope.

Retry 1 reached DWF target re-entry but the historical ValidateM1Gate rejected the newer 0.1.26 plan. Retry 2 runs this 0.1.25-specific gate only on baseline; the target re-entry checks pinned M1 evidence plus the read-only M2 IR/plan validators.
declared.nextAction: Implement M2-W01-C02 with independent REDs for exact vs approximate values, distinct bound/free symbols and the real sqrt(x²) domain restriction; create the first real IR project only with runnable green consumer/tests.

achievements.achievement: The first study question freezes comparison criteria for OpenMath 2.0 Revision 2, W3C Content MathML 4 and native/provider ASTs, including rational/quantity/matrix/function/exclusion semantics.

A five-case structured fidelity-and-loss matrix records exact values, unit identities, two-dimensional matrix shape, named operation arity, and the x != 1 exclusion plus explicit unsupported mappings.
The ADR selects a minimal immutable provider-neutral typed AST and treats OpenMath/MathML as optional future adapters rather than adopting an unbounded interchange language as an internal engine.
The study contract completes with researched standards, a five-case guarded mapping, explicit scope and a reasoned bounded typed IR decision without claiming an implemented library.
Boundary questions require stable symbol binding, retained assumptions, exact/approximate distinction, explicit complex/NaN/interval policy and rejection of a second unqualified BigRational core.
Current ExactRational and DimensionVector semantics, source parser bounds and M1 release proof are reviewed; proposed IR limits are distinguished from implemented enforcement.

The architecture rejects implicit numeric widening, unsafe symbolic simplification and dynamic function registries; it chooses ExactRational reuse with explicit bindings, restrictions and deferred complex/interval semantics.
The IR boundary decision closes with validated immutable-scope/assumption policies, a prospective resource budget and read-only schema checks, without creating any empty project.
The complete M2 IR architecture spike is qualified by a reasoned ADR, exact five-case OpenMath/MathML mapping ledger, and standalone read-only C# validator; the subsequent code chunk remains planned.
